title: Nephrology Fellowship
inst: Baylor College of Medicine
Department: Section of Nephrology, Department of Medicine
Duration: 2 years (clinical track) or 3 years (mentored research track)
Deadline: Not stated on official page
Eligibility: Must be authorized to work in the US; currently enrolled in or completed an ACGME or ACGME-I accredited internal medicine residency.
International applicants: J-1 visa holders are eligible to apply; applicants on H-1B status are not eligible. BCM International Services Office answers visa questions.
Funding: Annual CME allowance for conferences/educational material
Visa support: J-1 only; H-1B not eligible
Summary: Broad clinical nephrology training preparing fellows for academic or private practice, with a two-year clinical track or a three-year mentored research track offering a Masters in Clinical Investigation.

title: Nephrology Fellowship
inst: University of Toledo College of Medicine and Life Sciences
Department: Department of Medicine, Division of Nephrology
Duration: 2 years (optional additional year of critical care training)
Deadline: Not stated on official page
Eligibility: Enrolled in or completed an ACGME-accredited internal medicine programme (or equivalent Canadian accreditation); ECFMG certification for IMGs; personal statement, three letters, transcripts, Dean's letter, USMLE/COMLEX transcripts.
International applicants: Accepted; ECFMG certification required.
Visa support: Sponsors both J-1 and H-1B visas
Summary: A two-year nephrology training programme with an option to complete a one-year critical care fellowship afterwards, including transplant exposure.

title: Nephrology Fellowship
inst: Marshall University Joan C. Edwards School of Medicine
Deadline: Not stated on official page
Eligibility: US and international medical graduates; USMLE scores >206; less than 5 years since medical school graduation; programme director's letter plus three faculty letters, USMLE Step 1-3 scores, CV, personal statement.
International applicants: US and international medical graduates considered.
Visa support: J-1 visa only (no H-1 visas accepted)
Summary: Nephrology fellowship at Marshall University accepting US and international medical graduates through ERAS.

title: Nephrology Fellowship
inst: University of Kansas School of Medicine
Department: Division of Nephrology and Hypertension (Jared Grantham Kidney Institute)
Deadline: Applications open 1 July for positions starting the following July; interviews August to end of October
Eligibility: Completed an accredited internal medicine residency; passed all three steps of USMLE/COMLEX; ECFMG status report for graduates of foreign medical schools.
International applicants: Foreign medical graduates considered (ECFMG status report required).
Visa support: Sponsors J-1 and H-1 visas for selected applicants
Summary: KU nephrology fellowship recruiting through ERAS and the NRMP, sponsoring J-1 and H-1 visas for selected applicants.

title: Nephrology Fellowship
inst: University of South Florida Morsani College of Medicine
Department: Division of Nephrology & Hypertension, Department of Internal Medicine
Deadline: Mid-October (programme application deadline); interviews September to early November
Eligibility: Graduate of an LCME/AOA-accredited North American school or full ECFMG certification; ACLS and/or PALS; USMLE composite of at least 460 on Steps 1 and 2 and passing Step 2CS and Step 3 on first attempt.
International applicants: IMGs who are not US citizens must have received a J-1 visa; a limited number of highly qualified J-1 and H-1B trainees accepted.
Visa support: Limited number of highly qualified J-1 and H-1B trainees
Licence requirement: Florida Board of Medicine unlicensed physician-in-training registration or full unrestricted Florida licence by start date
Summary: USF nephrology fellowship that recruits via ERAS and the NRMP and will consider a limited number of highly qualified J-1 and H-1B trainees.

title: Nephrology Fellowship
inst: Boston University Chobanian & Avedisian School of Medicine / Boston Medical Center
Deadline: Not stated on official page
Eligibility: MD (or equivalent) and completed internal medicine residency; ECFMG certification for IMGs.
International applicants: IMGs accepted with ECFMG certification.
Application method: ERAS; NRMP (rank as Nephrology/Other); clinical-research track possible after year 1
Visa support: Offers both H-1B and J-1 visas to qualified applicants
Summary: Boston University nephrology fellowship accepting four clinical fellows a year, with flexibility to move onto a clinical-research track after the first year.

title: Nephrology Fellowship
inst: Olive View-UCLA Medical Center
Deadline: ERAS timeline: programmes receive applications from 15 July 2026; NRMP rank list deadline 18 November 2026; Match Day 2 December 2026
Eligibility: Completion of an ACGME-approved internal medicine residency in the United States before starting.
International applicants: Not stated on official page
Visa support: Not stated on official page
Summary: A two-year nephrology fellowship based at an academic county hospital in Los Angeles, with UCLA ties for kidney transplant training and community partners for outpatient haemodialysis.

title: Nephrology Fellowship
inst: Allegheny Health Network (Allegheny General Hospital)
Duration: 2 years (nephrology) or 3 years (combined nephrology/critical care track)
Deadline: Not stated on official page
Eligibility: Not stated on official page
International applicants: Not stated on official page
Visa support: Not stated on official page
Summary: A two-year ACGME-accredited nephrology fellowship established in 1974 covering consultative nephrology, dialysis including home haemodialysis, hypertension and transplant nephrology, with a combined nephrology-critical care track.

title: Nephrology Fellowship
inst: West Virginia University School of Medicine
Department: Section of Nephrology, Department of Medicine
Deadline: ERAS applications accepted mid-August through 15 October
Eligibility: Completing or completed an ACGME-approved internal medicine residency; ABIM board eligible; USMLE/COMLEX scores.
International applicants: Not stated on official page
Application method: ERAS only; combined Nephrology/Critical Care fellowship applied for separately in ERAS
Visa support: J-1 visas only; H-1B not sponsored
Summary: WVU nephrology fellowship recruiting two fellows per year through ERAS, also offering a combined nephrology/critical care fellowship.

title: Nephrology Fellowship
inst: University of Iowa Carver College of Medicine
Department: Division of Nephrology, Department of Internal Medicine
Deadline: 15 September; interviews early August to end of October
Eligibility: MD (or equivalent); completion or expected completion of three years of internal medicine residency with ABIM board eligibility or certification by the start of fellowship.
International applicants: Not stated on official page
Funding: Hotel accommodation reimbursed for interviewed candidates
Visa support: Sponsors J-1 visas; does not accept H-1B visas
Summary: University of Iowa Health Care nephrology fellowship recruiting through ERAS and the NRMP, sponsoring J-1 visas.

title: BWH/MGH Joint Nephrology Fellowship
inst: Brigham and Women's Hospital / Massachusetts General Hospital (Mass General Brigham)
Department: Mass General Brigham Nephrology (Harvard Medical School affiliated)
Deadline: ERAS opens 1 July; programme begins reviewing applications 15 July 2026; virtual interviews September-October
Eligibility: Three letters of reference including one from the internal medicine programme director.
International applicants: Visa sponsorship available for exceptional candidates.
Visa support: Sponsors H-1B or J-1 visas for exceptional fellowship candidates
Summary: A joint Harvard-affiliated nephrology fellowship combining rigorous clinical training across several sites with mentored research and subspecialty exposure in women's health, interventional nephrology, onconephrology, glomerular disease and genetics.

title: Nephrology Fellowship (Minnesota)
inst: Mayo Clinic College of Medicine and Science — Rochester
Deadline: Not stated on official page
Eligibility: Completed general internal medicine training by appointment date and qualified to take the ABIM certifying exam; transcripts and dean's letter sent to Mayo Clinic School of Graduate Medical Education.
International applicants: Open to international applicants; graduates of schools outside US/Canada must be ECFMG certified.
Visa support: Supports ECFMG J-1 sponsorship; H-1B only when J-1 is unavailable or the fellow already holds H-1B status for GME elsewhere
Licence requirement: All applicable licensure eligibility requirements must be fulfilled before starting
Summary: Mayo Clinic's Rochester nephrology fellowship offers four first-year positions a year and is open to US and international applicants.

title: Adult Nephrology Training Program
inst: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill School of Medicine
Deadline: Interviews late July through end of October
Eligibility: USMLE or COMLEX scores; ECFMG certificate if applicable.
International applicants: ECFMG-certified graduates may apply.
Visa support: J-1 visas considered for sponsorship; H-1B not offered
Summary: UNC's adult nephrology fellowship recruits through ERAS and the NRMP and considers J-1 visa sponsorship.

title: General Nephrology Fellowship Training Program
inst: University of Maryland School of Medicine
Deadline: ERAS from 1 July; applications encouraged complete by early August; Exceptional Candidate Pathway interviews must be complete by 30 September
Eligibility: Three letters (including residency programme director); personal statement. Graduates of ACGME-I or RCPSC internal medicine programmes, or a minimum 3-year IM residency abroad with exceptional qualifications, may apply via the Exceptional Candidate Pathway.
International applicants: Non-ACGME-trained applicants may apply through an Exceptional Candidate Pathway (contact coordinator).
Application method: ERAS; NRMP Medical Specialties Matching Program
Visa support: Sponsors J-1 visas for qualified candidates; does not sponsor H-1B
Summary: UMSOM general nephrology fellowship participating in ERAS/NRMP with an Exceptional Candidate Pathway for internationally trained internists.

title: Nephrology Fellowship
inst: University of Cincinnati College of Medicine / UC Medical Center
Department: Division of Nephrology and Hypertension, Department of Internal Medicine
Deadline: ERAS application during July-August recruitment season
Eligibility: MD or DO; US citizen, permanent resident, or H-1B/J-1 status; 3 years of US ACGME-accredited internal medicine training by entry; passed USMLE Steps 1-3.
International applicants: Eligible if holding H-1B or J-1 status and US ACGME IM training completed.
Visa support: H-1B or J-1 visa status accepted per eligibility criteria
Summary: University of Cincinnati nephrology fellowship filling positions through ERAS and the NRMP.

title: Renal Transplant Nephrology Fellowship
inst: University of Alabama at Birmingham (UAB) Heersink School of Medicine
Deadline: Rolling review; applicants needing visa support should apply 6-9 months before anticipated start
Eligibility: Completion of an ACGME-accredited US internal medicine residency and nephrology fellowship; board eligible/certified in IM and nephrology; at least two years of prior US ACGME-accredited training; US citizen/permanent resident or H-1B/J-1.
International applicants: Accepted if US ACGME-trained; supports H-1B applicants and exceptional J-1 applicants.
Accreditation: AST Transplant Nephrology Fellowship Training Accreditation Program; graduates meet UNOS transplant physician criteria
Application method: Direct application to the division (see programme page)
Visa support: H-1B and exceptional J-1 applicants supported
Summary: A one-year AST-accredited renal transplant nephrology fellowship at a centre performing 250-350 kidney transplants a year, qualifying graduates as UNOS-certified transplant physicians.

title: Interventional Nephrology Fellowship
inst: University of Alabama at Birmingham (UAB) Heersink School of Medicine
Deadline: Not stated on official page
Eligibility: Completed ACGME-accredited internal medicine residency and nephrology fellowship; board eligible/certified; at least two years of prior US ACGME-accredited training; all USMLE steps completed at application.
International applicants: Accepted if US ACGME-trained; programme supports qualified J-1 and H-1B sponsorship.
Application method: ERAS (code 1007148F0); no documents accepted outside ERAS
Visa support: Qualified J-1 and H-1B visa sponsorship
Licence requirement: Must be eligible for Alabama medical licence, Alabama Controlled Substance Certificate and federal DEA registration
Summary: A one-year interventional nephrology fellowship at UAB covering haemodialysis access and peritoneal catheter placement across a 1,200-bed academic medical campus.

title: Nephrology Transplant Fellowship
inst: Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis (Barnes-Jewish Hospital)
Deadline: Not stated on official page
Eligibility: Completion of an ACGME-accredited nephrology training programme; internal medicine residency outside the US acceptable for selected candidates.
International applicants: Internal medicine residency outside the US acceptable for selected candidates.
Positions: Two transplant fellows and one possible research fellow annually
Visa support: J-1 and H-1 visa support offered
Summary: A comprehensive high-volume renal and pancreas transplant nephrology fellowship at the Washington University/Barnes-Jewish Transplant Center with HLA lab, transplant pathology and research exposure.

title: Transplant Nephrology Fellowship
inst: UT Southwestern Medical Center
Department: Division of Nephrology, Department of Internal Medicine
Deadline: Applications accepted September through January
Eligibility: Board-eligible or certified in nephrology; CV, personal statement and three letters of reference.
International applicants: Foreign medical graduates must be ECFMG-certified and eligible for J-1 visa sponsorship.
Application method: Submit CV, personal statement and three references to the programme
Funding: PGY-6 salary and benefits plus allowance for books, travel and American Transplant Congress attendance
Visa support: J-1 (ECFMG)
Summary: A one-year transplant nephrology fellowship with seven dedicated transplant nephrologists, covering living donor and recipient care, transplant immunology, pathology and organ procurement.

title: Transplant Nephrology Fellowship
inst: University of Washington School of Medicine
Deadline: 2027-2028 position filled; review for 2028-2029 begins Spring 2027
Eligibility: US board-certified or board-eligible in nephrology; eligible for Washington medical licensure; three references including nephrology fellowship programme director.
International applicants: Only US citizens, permanent residents or J-1 holders considered.
Application method: Email documents to programme administrator and programme director
Visa support: J-1 only; cannot consider applicants needing H-1B sponsorship
Licence requirement: Eligible for medical licensure in Washington State
Summary: University of Washington transplant nephrology fellowship for US board-eligible nephrologists, recruiting by direct application.

title: Renal Transplant Fellowship (Florida)
inst: Mayo Clinic College of Medicine and Science — Florida
Deadline: Not stated on official page
Eligibility: Eligible for or holding ABIM certification and completed a general nephrology fellowship (US or abroad); foreign candidates must have completed US (or equivalent) ACGME IM training or 3 years under ABIM-certified faculty to sit ABIM boards.
International applicants: Foreign nationals who have or qualify for visa sponsorship may apply; ECFMG certificate required for non-US graduates.
Visa support: J-1 (nonstandard programme) available; H-1B requires USMLE Steps 1, 2CK, 2CS and 3 and completion within the six-year H-1B limit
Licence requirement: Eligibility for Florida medical licensure (for H-1B)
Summary: Mayo Clinic Jacksonville's renal transplant fellowship offers two competitive positions a year to nephrologists trained in the US or abroad.

title: Interventional Nephrology Fellowship
inst: University of Wisconsin School of Medicine and Public Health
Department: Division of Nephrology, Department of Medicine
Deadline: Rolling until positions fill; submit by end of September to ensure consideration
Eligibility: Completed general nephrology fellowship; CV, cover letter and three references including the nephrology fellowship programme director.
International applicants: Not stated on official page
Accreditation: American Society of Diagnostic and Interventional Nephrology (ASDIN)
Visa support: Not stated on official page
Summary: Widely regarded as a pioneer of interventional nephrology training, this dedicated one-year programme in a high-volume procedure centre prepares fellows for ASDIN certification in haemodialysis vascular access and PD catheter placement.

title: Interventional Nephrology Fellowship
inst: LSU Health Shreveport
Department: Section of Nephrology, School of Medicine
Deadline: 1 October; interviews October-November; contract signing end of December
Eligibility: Completed nephrology fellowship and board certified in internal medicine; certificates of IM residency and nephrology training (or nephrology board pass).
International applicants: Open to US citizens, green card holders and FMGs on J-1 visas with prior US training; J-1 holders with no prior US medical training are not candidates.
Accreditation: Not ACGME-accredited; ASDIN-approved curriculum (fellows eligible for ASDIN certification on meeting procedure numbers)
Visa support: J-1 only; H-1B holders not supported
Licence requirement: Must meet LSBME requirements for a fellowship training permit
Summary: One of the earliest US interventional nephrology programmes, offering a one-year hands-on fellowship in dialysis access care with simulation training and ASDIN-aligned didactics.
